name: Tevrna Net Profit for WooCommerce
author: tevrna

sections.description:
Your WooCommerce sales report shows revenue. Tevrna Net Profit shows what you actually keep.

For every order it takes the money you received, then subtracts the cost of the products, what you paid to ship it, the payment processor’s fee, refunds and any other costs you add. The result is your net profit per order, per product and per period, on one clear dashboard.

It runs entirely inside your WordPress site. No account and no monthly fee are needed, and your orders, costs and reports never leave your server.

What you get

  • Profit dashboard: net revenue, net profit, margin, orders, cost of goods, shipping costs, payment fees and profit per order, each compared with the previous period.
  • Revenue and profit chart by day, week or month.
  • Where your revenue goes: one bar showing how much of each sale goes to products, shipping, fees and profit.
  • Most and least profitable products, with a full sortable Products report.
  • Orders report with the profit and margin of every order, and a filter for orders with missing product costs.
  • Profit column in the WooCommerce orders list.
  • Net Profit box on each order with the full breakdown, plus fields for the real shipping cost and other costs of that order.
  • CSV export of the Orders and Products reports.
  • Setup checklist that tells you exactly what is missing for accurate numbers.

Accurate costs

  • Product costs come from WooCommerce’s built-in Cost of Goods Sold feature. The cost saved on each order line is used, so changing a product’s cost later does not rewrite past orders.
  • Costs from other plugins: if a product has no WooCommerce cost, the plugin can read the cost saved by other popular cost-of-goods plugins.
  • Real payment fees are read from WooCommerce Stripe Gateway, WooPayments and WooCommerce PayPal Payments when they record them. Otherwise your own rule (percent plus fixed fee) is used, and offline methods such as bank transfer and cash on delivery can be set to no fee.
  • Shipping costs use your rule (a flat cost per shipped order plus a share of the shipping charged), or the real cost you type on the order.
  • Refunds are taken out of revenue. You choose whether refunded items come back to stock or count as a loss.
  • Taxes are left out: revenue and costs are shown without tax.

Built for real stores

  • Compatible with High-Performance Order Storage (HPOS) and the classic posts storage.
  • Profit is stored in two small, indexed tables, so reports stay fast on stores with many orders.
  • Past orders are calculated in the background with WooCommerce’s own Action Scheduler.
  • New, edited and refunded orders update automatically.
  • Developers can add costs through filters such as tevrna_np_order_extra_cost, tevrna_np_order_breakdown and tevrna_np_period_totals.

Pro

The free plugin is complete for profit per order, product and period. Tevrna Net Profit Pro adds the costs that live outside your orders, so the profit you see is the money you actually keep:

  • Ad spend and return on ad spend: enter or import daily spend from Facebook, Google, TikTok or any channel.
  • Monthly fixed costs such as rent, software and staff, spread over the days they cover.
  • Fee and shipping rules per method: a different payment fee per gateway and shipping cost per shipping method or zone.
  • Return costs on refunds that send items back.
  • Bulk cost editor for every product and variation, with CSV import and export.
  • Profit by category, coupon, country and payment method, plus customer profit and repeat-customer value.
  • Scheduled email reports every week or month.
  • Multi-currency totals with your own exchange rates.

Pro comes with a free trial. Open the Pro tab under WooCommerce > Net Profit to start it.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate WooCommerce.
  2. Upload the tevrna-net-profit folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install the plugin from the Plugins screen.
  3. Activate the plugin. Past orders start calculating in the background.
  4. Go to WooCommerce > Net Profit and follow the setup checklist.
  5. Turn on WooCommerce > Settings > Advanced > Features > Cost of Goods Sold if it is off, then add a cost to your products.
sections.faq:
Where do I enter product costs?

Turn on WooCommerce’s Cost of Goods Sold feature under WooCommerce > Settings > Advanced > Features. A Cost field then appears on every product and variation. If you already use another cost-of-goods plugin, keep “Costs from other plugins” on in the settings and those costs are read too.

What happens to products without a cost?

They are counted at zero cost and flagged with a “No cost” badge so you can fix them. If you prefer, set an estimated cost as a percent of the selling price in the settings.

How are payment fees calculated?

When Stripe, WooPayments or PayPal Payments record the real fee on the order, that fee is used. Otherwise the plugin uses the percent and fixed fee you set. Payment methods you mark as “No fee” are never charged a fee.

Does it include tax?

No. Revenue, refunds and costs are shown without tax, because tax is money you collect for the government.

I changed some settings. Do I need to do anything?

When you change a setting that affects the math, past orders are recalculated automatically in the background. After adding product costs, use “Recalculate all orders” in the settings so older orders without a saved cost pick up the new costs.

Does it work with multiple currencies?

Reports add up orders in your store currency. Orders in other currencies are counted and shown in a note but not added to the totals. Pro lets you set exchange rates so those orders are converted and added.

Does the plugin send data anywhere?

Your orders, costs and reports never leave your server, and all calculations happen there.

The first time you open the plugin, it asks whether you want to opt in to security and feature update notices through Freemius, the service that handles our licensing and updates. Only if you opt in, Freemius receives basic details about your site and your WordPress user, such as the site address, WordPress and PHP versions, plugin version, and your name and email. If you choose Skip, nothing is sent and the plugin works exactly the same.

Will deleting the plugin remove my data?

Only if you tick “Delete all Net Profit data when the plugin is deleted” in the settings. Otherwise your data stays, so you can reinstall without recalculating.
sections.changelog:
1.1.0

  • New: Pro version with ad spend, fixed costs, cost rules per method, return costs, a bulk cost editor, breakdowns, customer profit, email reports and multi-currency totals.
  • New: optional opt-in for security and feature update notices. Skipping it changes nothing.
  • New: filters for add-ons, including tevrna_np_period_totals, tevrna_np_dashboard_cards and tevrna_np_fee_rule.
  • Improved: when a loss is involved, the dashboard shows the change in money instead of a percentage.
  • Improved: the order box says which currency its cost fields use.
  • Improved: deleting the plugin with “Delete all data” on also removes its temporary data.

1.0.0

  • First release.
